intro: Buffalo sits alone at 7-1 after a Monday night win in Minnesota, and Kansas City is waiting on word about Patrick Mahomes' throwing elbow. Giants and Commanders open Week 10 tonight on Prime Video, and the Saints and Panthers meet Sunday with first place in a four-way NFC South tie at stake. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Bills smother Vikings 23-6 to reach 7-1
top.dek: Buffalo held the ball for 42:32 on Monday night and forced three turnovers. Minnesota went 0-for-7 on third down. The Bills have won four straight and visit the Jets on Sunday.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Mahomes day to day with a sore throwing elbow
top.dek: Andy Reid said David Bailey's hit late in the first half left Mahomes sore and called the news more positive than negative. Receiver Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and tackle Jaylen Moore (ankle) are also day to day. Kansas City visits Atlanta on Sunday.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Jordan Love throws for 372 and accounts for four scores
top.dek: Love threw three touchdowns and ran for another in Green Bay's 45-27 win at New England. Christian Watson (171 yards) and Matthew Golden (164) each topped 150 yards and scored. The Packers have won five of their last six.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 5: turnovers in a Bears win, the first since 2006
top.dek: Chicago gave the ball away five times and still beat Tampa Bay 27-24 on a last-second Cairo Santos field goal. It was the Bears' fourth straight win. They are on bye this week.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Panthers visit Saints with first place in the NFC South up for grabs
top.dek: Both teams are 3-5 and every club in the division has three wins. Carolina plays at New Orleans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The winner takes sole possession of first.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills grind down Vikings, win fourth straight

stories.text: Bills smother Vikings 23-6 on Monday night for a fourth straight win
stories.summary: Buffalo improved to 7-1 at U.S. Bank Stadium by controlling the ball for 42:32 and holding Minnesota to 17:28 of possession. The defense forced three turnovers, including interceptions by Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard, and the Vikings went 0-for-7 on third down.

stories.text: Dawkins and Anderson sat out Monday night, replacements held up
stories.summary: Left tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs) and guard Alec Anderson (ankle) missed the Vikings game after sitting out practice Thursday and Friday. Tylan Grable and Austin Corbett filled in. Their status for the Jets game is not yet known.

stories.text: James Cook carries 31 times for 107 yards and a score
stories.summary: Cook ran for a 5-yard touchdown and powered a 15-play, 8:32 fourth-quarter drive that was Buffalo's longest of the season. He has a rushing touchdown and at least 75 yards in seven straight games, a team record, and he passed 5,000 career rushing yards on the same drive as Josh Allen.

stories.text: 0-for-7: Minnesota's third-down mark against Buffalo
stories.summary: The Vikings never moved the chains on third down, and Carson Wentz finished 8 of 25 for 81 yards with two interceptions. Josh Allen was a modest 21 of 31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one pick, because the run game and defense did the heavy work.

stories.text: Bills visit the Jets on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo plays at MetLife Stadium in Week 10, then returns home to face Miami in Week 11. Watch the status of Dawkins and Anderson up front against a Jets pass rush led by rookie David Bailey.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins fall 19-9 to Lions, sink to 1-7

stories.text: Dolphins drop to 1-7 after a 19-9 loss to Detroit
stories.summary: Miami went 0-for-3 in the red zone, took 11 penalties for 87 yards and missed a field goal. The youngest roster in the league insists it is done using youth as an excuse. Rookie Chris Johnson picked off Jared Goff in the first quarter for his first career interception.

stories.text: Malik Willis plays through a groin problem that lingers
stories.summary: Willis said his groin felt a little tight after the Lions game and answered Lord willing when asked if he would be better for Indianapolis. Tight end Will Kacmarek hurt his quad on a low hit in the third quarter and walked off on his own. Jeff Hafley was set to update Willis on Wednesday, and no official designation has been published.

stories.text: Chop Robinson and Josh Uche bother Goff with three first-half sacks
stories.summary: Miami's pass rushers kept Detroit's top-ranked offense to field goals until Jahmyr Gibbs scored late in the third quarter. On the other side, rookie receiver Caleb Douglas caught six passes for 70 yards.

stories.text: 11: penalties Miami committed for 87 yards
stories.summary: Willis was 13 of 25 for 128 yards and an interception, and Miami has failed to rush for 100 yards in back-to-back games. Detroit also ran a fake punt in the second quarter that caught the Dolphins off guard.

stories.text: Dolphins visit the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami plays at Indianapolis in Week 10. The first thing to watch is whether Willis, hampered by the groin, can run the way he did earlier this season. The Dolphins then travel to Buffalo in Week 11.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots routed by Packers before Munich trip

stories.text: Packers hang 45 on Patriots in 45-27 blowout at Gillette
stories.summary: Green Bay outgained New England 166-13 in the first quarter and scored 17 points in the third. Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns, and Drake Maye threw three first-half interceptions. The Patriots sit at 5-4, second in the AFC East, and would hold the No. 7 seed.

stories.text: Stevenson, Campbell and Ben Brown all left with knee injuries
stories.summary: Rhamondre Stevenson's MRI results were still pending Monday, and Will Campbell and Ben Brown also hurt knees against Green Bay. Receiver A.J. Brown, who has missed six games, may not make the trip to Germany, and Mike Vrabel said there was no decision yet. The team is considering activating Greg Van Roten from injured reserve.

stories.text: DeMario Douglas posts a career-high 102 receiving yards
stories.summary: Douglas caught five passes for his second 100-yard game. Mack Hollins returned from injured reserve to start and scored on a 22-yard catch, and Corey Kiner ran for his first NFL touchdown while leading the team with 55 rushing yards.

stories.text: 6: straight games with three touchdowns for Drake Maye
stories.summary: Maye threw three touchdown passes and 299 yards against Green Bay, extending a run that is the second longest in team history behind Tom Brady in 2007. He also passed Jim Plunkett for fifth on the franchise list with 64 career touchdown passes.

stories.text: Patriots face the Lions in Munich on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Week 10 game is at Allianz Arena, so the team leaves Wednesday, a day early, with a walkthrough Thursday and practice Friday. Watch the secondary, which gave up 335 yards to Green Bay's two top receivers.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets lose fourth straight, 35-12 at Kansas City

stories.text: Chiefs bury Jets 35-12 as the skid hits four games
stories.summary: Kenneth Walker scored three touchdowns and ran for 102 yards as Kansas City pulled away. The Jets, now 2-7, scored only on field goals, and Aaron Glenn said the defense did not hold up against the run. His job security is drawing growing pressure.

stories.text: Garrett Wilson missed the Chiefs game, Breece Hall returned
stories.summary: Wilson was ruled out in the concussion protocol after a helmet-to-helmet hit against the Raiders and missed a third straight practice that Friday. Hall came back from a five-game quad injury. Wilson's status for Buffalo has not been announced.

stories.text: Adonai Mitchell is the deep threat to watch
stories.summary: Mitchell caught the ball for a career-high 142 yards and a touchdown against Las Vegas after missing four games with a finger injury. He leads the team with nine deep targets, and his role grows if Wilson stays out.

stories.text: 5: sacks Kansas City took on Geno Smith
stories.summary: Smith finished with 165 passing yards. Hall and Braelon Allen combined for 94 rushing yards, and the offense never reached the end zone.

stories.text: Jets host the Bills on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo comes to MetLife Stadium at 7-1 in Week 10. Watch whether Wilson clears the protocol and whether the run defense improves.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens lose a fourth straight, 33-10

stories.text: Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 for Baltimore's fourth straight loss
stories.summary: Baltimore fell to 4-5 on Thursday night, the first time in team history it has lost three straight games by 20 or more points. Jesse Minter pointed to an explosive play before halftime that broke the game open and called the pre-snap penalties unacceptable. The Ravens had four more false starts and now lead the league with 24.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson on IR as Hamilton's hip check awaits
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve with a right thumb injury, and Minter will not say whether he needs surgery. Safety Kyle Hamilton left Thursday's game with a hip injury, and Minter said things look fairly good, with more clarity coming once players return Tuesday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) has missed three straight games, and cornerback Nate Wiggins (illness) sat out against Jacksonville.

stories.text: Derrick Henry moves up to seventh on the career rushing list
stories.summary: Henry carried 17 times for 57 yards against Jacksonville, enough to pass another back and take seventh place on the all-time rushing list. The Ravens still ran the Wildcat 10 times and attempted just one pass of 10 or more yards downfield, so the ground game carried a stalled offense.

stories.text: 24: false starts for Baltimore, the most in the league
stories.summary: Four more flags before the snap against Jacksonville pushed the Ravens to a league-high 24 false starts this season. Rookie Joe Fagnano, making his first career start on a heavily wrapped ankle, went 10 for 18 for 60 yards with two interceptions, and Baltimore's longest completion was 14 yards.

stories.text: Ravens host Chargers on Monday night with Brissett at QB
stories.summary: Baltimore plays the Chargers at home on Monday, Nov. 16, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Jacoby Brissett, acquired in a trade with Arizona, is expected to start, and Minter said he will get the ball out on time. Watch whether the offense stretches the field after the Jaguars game and whether Hamilton is back.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals take Madrid, win four straight

stories.text: Bengals beat Falcons 34-17 in Madrid for a fourth straight win
stories.summary: Cincinnati improved to 6-2 with its first victory outside the United States. Joe Burrow went 24 of 29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns, with no interceptions, and added a 1-yard sneak for a score. The Bengals now host Pittsburgh with a share of the AFC North lead.

stories.text: Dugger out week to week with a quad injury
stories.summary: At the Madrid practice on Nov. 5, safety Kyle Dugger (quad) did not practice and is week to week. Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) went from out Wednesday to full Thursday, defensive end Cedric Johnson (ankle and foot) was limited, and safety Jordan Battle (hamstring) was limited both days. The Bengals have not published a post-trip report for the Steelers game in what I found.

stories.text: Ja'Marr Chase puts up 155 yards in Spain
stories.summary: Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a 47-yard touchdown against Atlanta, and Tee Higgins added five catches and two scores. Burrow said afterward he would have a hard time putting anybody above Chase.

stories.text: 3: straight touchdown drives to open the Madrid game
stories.summary: Cincinnati scored on its first three possessions after two games of slow starts, finishing with 34 points and 123 rushing yards. Chase had 8 catches for 142 yards in the first half alone, the best first half by a Bengal since 1988, and Chase Brown ran nine times for 57.

stories.text: Bengals host Steelers on Sunday night with the division on the line
stories.summary: Cincinnati hosts Pittsburgh on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Both teams are 6-2 with four-game win streaks, and the Steelers won the first meeting 30-27. Watch the travel angle: teams coming off an international game are 0-5 the next week against opponents coming off a bye.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns fall in OT after missed 2-point try

stories.text: Saints beat Browns 23-22 in overtime after failed 2-point try
stories.summary: Cleveland dropped to 5-4 after Tyler Shough's New Orleans team scored first in overtime. Harold Fannin Jr. answered with a 39-yard touchdown catch, and the Browns went for two and the win, but Shedeur Sanders was pressured, rolled right and threw incomplete. Andre Szmyt's 51-yard field goal had forced overtime.

stories.text: Watson cleared and set to start against Texans
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson cleared the concussion protocol Saturday but was inactive against the Saints, and the Browns plan to start him Sunday against his former team, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Todd Monken praised Sanders but would not discuss the quarterback job beyond that.

stories.text: KC Concepcion scores first NFL touchdown on a 64-yard catch
stories.summary: The rookie receiver caught four passes for 85 yards, including the 64-yard score late in the fourth quarter that put Cleveland ahead. He left in the third quarter with an injury and returned at the start of the fourth.

stories.text: 2: 60-yard completions from Sanders, double Watson's total
stories.summary: Sanders threw two completions of 60 or more yards against New Orleans, twice as many as Watson had in his first eight starts. He finished 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns in his first start of the year. Watson entered Week 9 ranked 28th of 30 qualifying quarterbacks in QBR.

stories.text: Browns host Texans on Sunday with Watson facing his old team
stories.summary: Cleveland plays Houston at home on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch Watson against the team that traded him, and whether the deep shots Sanders hit return to the offense.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers rest at 6-2, then visit Bengals

stories.text: Steelers return from bye at 6-2 with Bengals up next
stories.summary: Pittsburgh enters the second half on a four-game win streak and tied with Cincinnati atop the AFC North. Mike McCarthy said the bye helped players recharge, and he left roster moves ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline to GM Omar Khan. The team returned to work Monday.

stories.text: Pittman, Wilson and Harmon stay on injured reserve
stories.summary: Receivers Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson remain on injured reserve with no timetable to return, and defensive lineman Derrick Harmon went on IR last month with a foot injury. I found no new designations during the bye.

stories.text: T.J. Watt sits at 7.5 sacks, tied for the NFL lead
stories.summary: Watt led a Pittsburgh pass rush that sacked Deshaun Watson eight times in the 27-6 win over Cleveland on Nov. 1. The Steelers lean on an aggressive scheme from coordinator Patrick Graham, and Watt will face Joe Burrow next.

stories.text: 23: sacks for Pittsburgh, most in the NFL, split across 10 players
stories.summary: No team has brought down quarterbacks more often than the Steelers, and the production is not one man's. Undrafted rookie tackle Kevin Jobity recorded his first career sack against Cleveland.

stories.text: Steelers visit Bengals on Sunday night for first place
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays at Paycor Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Steelers won the first meeting 30-27, then travel to Philadelphia and host Denver the Friday after Thanksgiving. Watch the pass rush against a Bengals offense that scored 34 in Madrid.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Stroud's five TDs spark a 44-22 rout

stories.text: Stroud throws five touchdowns as Texans rout winless Chargers 44-22
stories.summary: Houston beat Los Angeles 44-22 at SoFi Stadium on Sunday and has won three of its last four after an 0-4 start. C.J. Stroud threw for 384 yards and five touchdowns, and the defense sacked Justin Herbert eight times. The Texans are 3-5 and next travel to Cleveland.

stories.text: Montgomery sits out again as Texans list 11 on Wednesday report
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday, and coach DeMeco Ryans calls him week-to-week. Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, tight end Brevin Jordan and guard Keylan Rutledge (neck and shoulder) also sat out. Receivers Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) and Tank Dell (hand and shoulder), back Woody Marks (knee) and safety Reed Blankenship (concussion) were limited.

stories.text: Stroud posts 384 yards and five scores, with Boutte and Dell on the end of long balls
stories.summary: Stroud completed 21 of 35 passes with one interception. Kayshon Boutte caught two touchdowns, including a 63-yarder in the fourth quarter, and Tank Dell scored his first touchdown in more than two years. Xavier Hutchinson opened the scoring with a 17-yard catch on the first drive.

stories.text: 8: sacks of Justin Herbert, a career high for the Chargers quarterback
stories.summary: Sheldon Rankins, Jadeveon Clowney and Will Anderson Jr. each took down Herbert twice. The defense also forced two turnovers, and the offense piled up 485 total yards.

stories.text: Texans visit Cleveland Sunday, then host the Colts on a short week
stories.summary: Houston plays at the Browns on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox at Huntington Bank Field. Watch the running back room, since Montgomery and Marks are both banged up. The Texans then host Indianapolis on Thursday night, Nov. 19, on Prime Video.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts sell off vets, then lose late to Dallas

stories.text: Colts sell Downs and Allen at the deadline but keep Jonathan Taylor
stories.summary: Indianapolis sent receiver Josh Downs to Kansas City for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks and moved Keenan Allen to San Francisco for a sixth. The Colts also dealt DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson since Oct. 27. They held onto Taylor, who drew second-round offers.

stories.text: Right tackle Jalen Travis hurt his knee against Dallas
stories.summary: Travis left the Cowboys game with a knee injury and is reported to miss two to four weeks. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies (neck) and tight end Mo Alie-Cox (groin) also left the game. Receiver Alec Pierce remains on injured reserve with a heel injury, and Shane Steichen would not set a return timetable.

stories.text: Daniel Jones throws for 180 yards as the offense stalls in a 27-23 loss
stories.summary: Jones managed 180 yards on 34 attempts and threw a game-ending interception on third down. Ashton Dulin caught a 55-yard touchdown on a screen. Jonathan Taylor carried 13 times for 46 yards and lost a fourth-quarter fumble.

stories.text: 1:37: the time left when the Colts took a 23-20 lead they could not hold
stories.summary: Spence Shrader's field goal put Indianapolis ahead, but Dallas answered on the next snap with a 47-yard gain and scored to win 27-23. CeeDee Lamb finished with 10 catches for 195 yards. It was the Colts' fifth straight loss.

stories.text: Colts host the 1-7 Dolphins Sunday, then play at Houston Thursday
stories.summary: Indianapolis hosts Miami on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Lucas Oil Stadium. Watch how a thinned receiver room moves the ball after the deadline trades. The Colts then visit the Texans on Thursday night, Nov. 19, on Prime Video.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars load up on defense before Titans trip

stories.text: Jaguars add Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux in three trades
stories.summary: Jacksonville acquired defensive tackle Jordan Davis from Philadelphia for a 2027 first and 2029 second. Safety Jessie Bates III cost a 2027 second and 2028 fifth from Atlanta, and Godchaux came from New Orleans for a conditional sixth. General manager James Gladstone rejected the all-in label and called the deals team building.

stories.text: Tuten, Meyers and Walker miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle and foot), receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle) and end Travon Walker (rib) did not practice. Davis and Bates sat out as veteran rest days. Center Robert Hainsey (concussion), guard Ezra Cleveland and safety Antonio Johnson were limited. Liam Coen has not said whether the new defenders play Sunday.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence stays sharp in a 33-10 win at Baltimore
stories.summary: Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown, a 50-yard strike to Parker Washington before halftime. He has 18 touchdown passes against four interceptions this season. Coen called his performance extremely sharp and accurate.

stories.text: 17: points the Jaguars defense has allowed in two games since the bye
stories.summary: Jacksonville held Baltimore to 10 points on Thursday night and forced three turnovers. Coen says his team leads the NFL in run defense, and the new tackles should help. The Jaguars lead the AFC South by 3.5 games.

stories.text: Jaguars visit the Titans Sunday in Nashville
stories.summary: Jacksonville plays at Tennessee on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox at Nissan Stadium. Watch how quickly Bates and the new tackles work into the defense. The Jaguars play at the Giants the following Sunday.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans deal Hooker, stockpile 2027 picks

stories.text: Titans trade Amani Hooker to Buffalo for a second-round pick
stories.summary: Tennessee sent the safety and a 2027 fifth-rounder to the Bills for a 2027 second. The Titans now hold two first-round and two second-round picks in next year's draft, after trading Jeffery Simmons to Chicago for two firsts. Hooker had five interceptions this season.

stories.text: Rookie receiver Carnell Tate misses Wednesday practice with a shoulder injury
stories.summary: Tate did not practice as the Titans began preparing for Jacksonville. The injury is about three weeks old, and he missed the Week 8 game at Cincinnati. Running back Tyjae Spears has a knee injury and missed the Cincinnati game.

stories.text: Cam Ward throws for 340 yards in a 43-36 overtime loss
stories.summary: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for two touchdowns, the first 300-yard game of his career. His 15-yard touchdown to Wan'Dale Robinson put Tennessee ahead late. Tony Pollard added 117 rushing yards and two scores, but the Titans lost in overtime.

stories.text: 413: receiving yards for rookie Carnell Tate through eight games, tops on the Titans
stories.summary: The fourth overall pick has 21 catches for 290 yards in October alone, plus a first career touchdown at Indianapolis. He is one of three Titans with 400 yards in his first seven rookie games, with Bill Groman and Ernest Givins. He earned the NFL's Offensive Rookie of the Month award.

stories.text: Titans host the 6-2 Jaguars Sunday after the bye
stories.summary: Tennessee plays Jacksonville on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox at Nissan Stadium. Watch whether the offense repeats its Cincinnati output against the league's top run defense. The Titans then visit Dallas on Nov. 22.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos win a fifth straight, then rest

stories.text: Broncos hold off Panthers 26-21 for a fifth straight win
stories.summary: Denver went to Charlotte and won a game that turned on two fourth-quarter plays. A Sean Payton challenge flipped a Carolina goal-line sequence into an interception, and Nik Bonitto's strip-sack with 1:24 left sealed it. The Broncos sit alone atop the AFC West at 7-2.

stories.text: Waddle and Moss leave Carolina game with concussions
stories.summary: Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle took a hit to the helmet on a catch attempt and went to the locker room, where doctors diagnosed a concussion. Cornerback Riley Moss also suffered one in the first half. Both were ruled out, and the bye week buys each of them extra time to clear the protocol.

stories.text: Bonitto's strip-sack ends it for Denver
stories.summary: Nik Bonitto forced and recovered a fumble from Bryce Young in the final two minutes, his first strip-sack of the season. Bo Nix then converted a third-down sneak to run out the clock. Nix finished with two touchdown passes, one of them to Pat Bryant in his first game back from injured reserve.

stories.text: 16: straight one-score wins, an NFL record
stories.summary: Denver has now won 16 consecutive regular-season games decided by one score, a league record. The Panthers game fit the pattern: the Broncos outscored Carolina 13-7 in the fourth quarter. Denver is 3-2 on the road this season.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then the Raiders at home
stories.summary: Denver has no game this weekend. The Broncos return on Sunday, Nov. 22 to host Las Vegas, and they will get a full two weeks to heal. Watch whether Waddle and Moss clear concussion protocol before that game.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs snap skid, Mahomes elbow in focus

stories.text: Chiefs rout Jets 35-12 to end a two-game skid
stories.summary: Kansas City scored a season-high 35 points and shook off a slow start. Kenneth Walker III scored three touchdowns, two on Patrick Mahomes passes, as the Chiefs improved to 6-2. Denver beat them 28-24 on Nov. 1.

stories.text: Mahomes day to day with elbow; Worthy, Moore also hurting
stories.summary: Andy Reid said Mahomes is day to day after David Bailey sacked him and hit the throwing elbow late in the first half. Reid called the news more positive than negative and described it as a soreness issue. Receiver Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and right tackle Jaylen Moore (ankle) are also day to day.

stories.text: Walker leads the league with 11 touchdowns
stories.summary: Kenneth Walker III ran for 102 yards and a score and finished with 143 yards from scrimmage against New York. The three-touchdown game was his third of his career. He now leads the NFL with 11 total touchdowns through eight games.

stories.text: 5: sacks by the Chiefs defense against New York
stories.summary: Chris Jones and George Karlaftis each had multiple sacks, and Karlaftis added three tackles for loss. The Jets gained just 46 yards in the second half. On offense, Kansas City went 4-for-4 in the red zone.

stories.text: At Atlanta on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Chiefs visit the 3-6 Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15. The big question is Mahomes' elbow, and how many of Worthy and Moore are ready.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Turnovers bury Raiders in Santa Clara

stories.text: Five second-half takeaways sink Raiders, 38-17
stories.summary: San Francisco forced five turnovers after halftime and pulled away from Las Vegas. Kirk Cousins threw three interceptions, including a 35-yard pick-six by Jaden Dugger, and Michael Mayer lost a fumble at the goal line. The Raiders fell to 4-5.

stories.text: Zuhn leaves with a concussion
stories.summary: Offensive lineman Trey Zuhn left in the second half with a concussion. He will need to clear the protocol this week before he can face Seattle. The recap did not list any other Raiders injuries.

stories.text: Bowers piles up 111 yards but fumbles
stories.summary: Brock Bowers caught seven passes for 111 yards and a 21-yard touchdown from Cousins. He also lost a fumble on a screen pass. It was a productive day for the tight end that still hurt in the turnover count.

stories.text: 3: Cousins interceptions, one for a touchdown
stories.summary: Cousins threw three picks, with Dugger returning the first for a score after a bobbled snap and an underthrow. Renardo Green took another away in the end zone in the fourth quarter. Cousins also ran in a 1-yard touchdown, his second straight week with a rushing score.

stories.text: Seahawks visit Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts Seattle on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Raiders need to clean up ball security after giving it away five times in the second half in Santa Clara. Watch the offensive line if Zuhn cannot go.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers fall 44-22 to Houston

stories.text: Texans beat Chargers 44-22 as L.A. falls to 0-8
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud threw five touchdown passes as Houston ran away with it. The Chargers lost their eighth straight game and tied a franchise record for consecutive losses. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel called plays from the booth for the first time this season.

stories.text: Herbert's finger may be fractured; McConkey out with back spasms
stories.summary: Justin Herbert left in the fourth quarter with an injury to the middle finger of his non-throwing left hand, and coach Jim Harbaugh said it could be a fracture. Herbert expects to play Monday. Ladd McConkey was active but did not play because of back spasms, and cornerback Isas Waxter hurt an ankle.

stories.text: Herbert takes eight sacks, throws for 193
stories.summary: Herbert went 13 of 23 for 193 yards with one interception and one touchdown, a 58-yard throw to Quentin Johnston. He took a career-high eight sacks, and he has been sacked 31 times this season, second most in the league. DJ Uiagalelei replaced him and threw his first career touchdown, a 15-yard pass to Derius Davis.

stories.text: 37: drives without a touchdown before Johnston's catch
stories.summary: Johnston's 58-yard score ended a 37-drive touchdown drought, described as the second longest in NFL history. It was the Chargers' first touchdown since Oct. 11 against Denver. In that stretch they scored 24 points on field goals.

stories.text: At Baltimore on Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: The Chargers visit the Ravens on Monday night, Nov. 16, and face former Chargers defensive coordinator Jesse Minter. Herbert's hand and the protection problems lead the watch list. Los Angeles has not won a game this season.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys edge Colts 27-23 on late Williams score

stories.text: Cowboys steal one from Indianapolis, 27-23
stories.summary: Javonte Williams plunged in from the 1-yard line with 1:08 left to put Dallas ahead of the Colts, and Caleb Downs sealed it with an interception of Daniel Jones with 35 seconds to play. It was the Cowboys' first win of the year when they scored fewer than 30 points. Dallas moved to 4-5 and now opens a three-game homestand.

stories.text: Ferguson, Goodson and Locke face multiple missed weeks
stories.summary: Tight end Jake Ferguson hurt his left knee against the Colts, and coach Brian Schottenheimer says he will miss multiple weeks. Running back Tyler Goodson also hurt a knee and is out for a stretch, while safety PJ Locke suffered his second concussion in two weeks and is out against the 49ers. George Pickens (hamstring), KaVontae Turpin (ribs), DeMarvion Overshown and Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) are in the rehab group, with their Sunday status still open.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb piles up 195 yards in Indianapolis
stories.summary: Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown, even with a lost fumble on his ledger. Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards and two scores, and Williams added 101 yards on 20 carries. With Pickens inactive, Lamb carried the receiver room.

stories.text: 508: Dallas outgained Indianapolis by 237 yards and barely won
stories.summary: The Cowboys piled up 508 yards to the Colts' 271, yet the game came down to the final minute. Dallas drew 14 penalties for 153 yards and lost two fumbles, one by Prescott that set up an Indianapolis touchdown. Clean those up and this offense wins by two scores.

stories.text: San Francisco visits AT&T Stadium Sunday
stories.summary: Dallas hosts the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox in Arlington. It opens a three-game homestand. Watch how the Cowboys fill the tight end spot with Ferguson out and whether Pickens returns from his hamstring injury.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Reese's three sacks power Giants past Eagles

stories.text: Giants beat Eagles 19-11 and lead the NFC East
stories.summary: New York went to Philadelphia and won 19-11 behind a season-high seven sacks and four field goals from rookie kicker Dominic Zvada. The defense held the Eagles to 220 yards and forced five three-and-outs. The Giants sit at 5-2-1 with the division lead and a Thursday night game at home.

stories.text: McCarthy's hip pointer looks manageable for Thursday
stories.summary: J.J. McCarthy left the Eagles game with a hip pointer after a third-quarter hit, then returned to finish 12 of 19 for 127 yards. Coach John Harbaugh said Monday that McCarthy looks like he will play and that he feels fairly good about it. McCarthy said a lot of guys are banged up after the physical game.

stories.text: Arvell Reese turns Philadelphia into his playground
stories.summary: The rookie linebacker finished with 12 tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble. His strip-sack of Joe Milton took 2.29 seconds, the fastest sack in the NFL this season by Next Gen Stats. Micah McFadden recovered the fumble and added nine tackles and a sack in place of the injured Tremaine Edmunds.

stories.text: 7: sacks of Joe Milton, a Giants season high
stories.summary: The Giants hit Milton seven times, held the Eagles to 5-of-18 on third down and pinned them inside the 20 five times with Jordan Stout punts. Milton finished 18 of 34 for 169 yards. Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards for Philadelphia.

stories.text: Washington visits MetLife tonight on Prime Video
stories.summary: The Giants host the Commanders tonight, Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video at MetLife Stadium. New York is 5-2-1 and Washington is 2-5-1. Watch McCarthy's hip and whether the pass rush keeps up its pace on a short week.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles hit the bye at 2-7 with staff questions

stories.text: Seven straight losses leave Sirianni weighing staff changes
stories.summary: The Eagles fell 19-11 to the Giants and head into the bye at 2-7, their seventh straight loss. Coach Nick Sirianni did not rule out coaching staff changes and said he has not done a good enough job on offense. That unit ranks 30th in the league at 16.4 points per game in play caller Sean Mannion's first season.

stories.text: Baun's back is the one injury note from Sunday
stories.summary: Linebacker Zack Baun hurt his back on the third-quarter play that sent Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy to the locker room, according to the Giants' game story. Philadelphia has not updated his status. PhillyVoice reported no Eagles injuries from the game, and Baun led the defense with two sacks. The bye gives the team time to sort it out.

stories.text: Joe Milton runs the offense but takes a beating
stories.summary: Milton, who has been with the team about three weeks, replaced Tanner McKee at quarterback. He went 18 of 34 for 169 yards while the Giants sacked him seven times. The offense gained 220 yards and scored one touchdown.

stories.text: 16.4: Eagles points per game, 30th in the NFL
stories.summary: Philadelphia's offense also ranks 28th in efficiency, and second-half adjustments have been a repeated problem. The bye gives Sirianni and Mannion two weeks to find a fix before Pittsburgh.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then the Steelers on Nov. 22
stories.summary: The Eagles are off this week. They return Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Lincoln Financial Field against Pittsburgh, which is 6-2. The NFL flexed the game out of the 4:25 p.m. window.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders fall to Rams 20-13, offense stalls

stories.text: Rams beat Washington 20-13 as late drive ends in a fumble
stories.summary: Los Angeles won in Landover after Myles Garrett returned from knee surgery with three sacks. Washington had 313 yards but went 3 of 12 on third down and scored three points after halftime. Dan Quinn said the team has not nailed its complementary football, pointing to two takeaways that produced only a field goal.

stories.text: Washington's injured list keeps growing before Thursday
stories.summary: Terry McLaurin, Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw and Dyami Brown are all on injured reserve. Guard Lucas Patrick is doubtful, and Fabian Moreau and Treylon Burks are questionable for the Giants game. McLaurin tore a patellar tendon on Oct. 19 and is done for the season.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels throws for 274 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Daniels completed 21 of 28 passes for 274 yards and a 7-yard touchdown to Van Jefferson. He passed 6,000 career passing yards and reached 40 career touchdown passes. Rachaad White added a 45-yard catch.

stories.text: 3 of 12: Washington's third-down mark against the Rams
stories.summary: The Commanders converted three of 12 third downs and allowed the Rams to convert all three fourth-down tries. Washington's defense gave up 343 yards, and its two takeaways produced one field goal. Quinn wants all three phases to work together.

stories.text: Short week: at the Giants tonight on Prime Video
stories.summary: Washington plays at MetLife Stadium tonight, Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video against the 5-2-1 Giants. The Commanders are 2-5-1 and sit well behind New York in the NFC East. Watch how they cover the receiver spot with McLaurin out.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears survive five turnovers, win four straight

stories.text: Bears beat Tampa Bay on a last-second field goal
stories.summary: Chicago turned the ball over five times and still beat the Buccaneers 27-24 at Soldier Field. The Bears led 17-3 at the half, then watched Tampa Bay tie it late. Caleb Williams hit Colston Loveland for 38 yards on the final drive, and Cairo Santos kicked a 38-yard field goal as time ran out. It was Chicago's fourth straight win.

stories.text: Burden in concussion protocol, Stevenson hurt
stories.summary: Receiver Luther Burden III left Sunday night with a concussion and is in the league protocol. The bye week gives him time to clear it. AP also reported cornerback Tyrique Stevenson hurt his thumb. Running back Kyle Monangai and defensive back Malik Muhammad are expected back after the break.

stories.text: Jaylon Johnson returns an interception 67 yards for a score
stories.summary: The Bears cornerback took a Baker Mayfield pass back 67 yards for a touchdown, the second pick-six of his career. Johnson's score helped Chicago build its early lead on a night when the offense gave the ball away five times. Mayfield threw two interceptions in the game.

stories.text: 5: turnovers in a Bears win, the first such win since 2006
stories.summary: Chicago gave the ball away five times, four of them Williams interceptions, and still won. The AP says it is the Bears' first victory with five or more turnovers since 2006. Williams finished 22 of 37 for 279 yards and two touchdowns. Ben Johnson said it is hard to win that way, and the team found a way anyway.

stories.text: Bye week, then the Saints at Soldier Field
stories.summary: Chicago is off in Week 10 after three straight primetime games. The Bears host New Orleans on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Watch whether the offense cleans up the turnovers and whether Burden clears the protocol.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions grind out a fourth straight win in Miami

stories.text: Lions win 19-9 in Miami without a big offensive day
stories.summary: Detroit beat the Dolphins 19-9 and never trailed, its fourth straight win. The league's top-ranked offense, which came in averaging 395.4 yards, finished with 271. Jake Bates kicked four field goals and the defense held Miami without a touchdown. Dan Campbell picked up his 54th win as Lions coach.

stories.text: Jack Campbell on injured reserve with neck injury
stories.summary: The Lions placed All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell on injured reserve on Saturday, less than a week after he was hospitalized with a neck injury against Minnesota. Dan Campbell said Friday that Jack continues to improve. Linebacker Jimmy Rolder is out for the season and needs surgery, per the coach's update last week. Detroit's players wore No. 46 jerseys on Sunday in tribute.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs scores on fourth down in Miami
stories.summary: Gibbs carried 20 times for 74 yards and ran in an 8-yard touchdown on fourth down, his 11th touchdown from scrimmage this season. Jameson Williams set it up with a 31-yard catch, Detroit's longest play of the day. Amon-Ra St. Brown added 86 receiving yards.

stories.text: 54: Dan Campbell's wins, second most in Lions history
stories.summary: Campbell's 54th regular-season win moved him into sole possession of second place on the franchise list in his sixth season. Only Wayne Fontes is ahead with 66 wins, from 1988 to 1996.

stories.text: Lions meet the Patriots in Munich
stories.summary: Detroit faces New England on Sunday, Nov. 15 at Allianz Arena in Munich. Kickoff is 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX. The Patriots arrive off a 45-27 loss to Green Bay, so watch how Detroit's offense bounces back and who steps up at linebacker.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers hang 45 on the Patriots in Foxborough

stories.text: Packers rout Patriots 45-27 behind Jordan Love
stories.summary: Green Bay beat New England 45-27 at Gillette Stadium and has won five of its last six. The defense forced four turnovers that turned into 21 points. The Patriots gave up a franchise-record 45 points at home. Green Bay gained 478 yards in all.

stories.text: Josh Jacobs needs surgery on fractured finger
stories.summary: Running back Josh Jacobs fractured the ring finger on his right hand in the first quarter and needs surgery. Matt LaFleur said Jacobs had no grip strength after trying tape and then a cast. Injured reserve is not ruled out, which would mean at least four games. Linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper left with a chest injury but LaFleur does not expect him to miss time.

stories.text: Jordan Love throws for 372 and accounts for four scores
stories.summary: Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns and added a rushing touchdown. Christian Watson caught seven passes for 171 yards and a score, and Matthew Golden had 10 for 164 and a touchdown. They are the first Packers teammates since 1942 to each top 150 receiving yards and score in the same game.

stories.text: 1962: last time Green Bay scored 45 with 450 yards
stories.summary: The Packers had not scored 45 or more points while gaining 450 or more yards since 1962. They did it Sunday despite entering the day last in the NFL in rushing offense. They ran for 129 yards, their first game this season above 86.

stories.text: Vikings visit Lambeau before the Week 11 bye
stories.summary: Green Bay hosts Minnesota on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at Lambeau Field, then takes its bye. Watch the running back room without Jacobs, and whether Kaleb Johnson, who ran for 68 yards on 14 carries Sunday, keeps the job.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings offense stalls in 23-6 loss to Bills

stories.text: Bills beat Vikings 23-6 on Monday night
stories.summary: Buffalo handled Minnesota 23-6 at U.S. Bank Stadium, dropping the Vikings to 6-2. Carson Wentz started in place of the injured Kyler Murray and threw two interceptions. James Cook ran 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown. Max Brosmer finished at quarterback.

stories.text: Kyler Murray's hamstring is a week-to-week issue
stories.summary: Murray strained his hamstring on a read-option run in the fourth quarter at Detroit and sat out Monday. Kevin O'Connell said the team hopes he can return for the Nov. 15 game at Green Bay but will evaluate him week to week. The Vikings are not considering injured reserve. Receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) and running back Demond Claiborne (knee) were also ruled out for the Bills game.

stories.text: Justin Jefferson held to three catches by Buffalo
stories.summary: Jefferson caught three passes for 58 yards against the Bills. With Wentz at quarterback this season he had averaged 6.4 catches and 89.1 yards over seven games, per the team's game preview. Minnesota's passing game managed 81 yards on Wentz's 8-of-25 night.

stories.text: 81: Carson Wentz's passing yards on 25 attempts
stories.summary: Wentz completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions against Buffalo. Brosmer went 6 of 7 for 58 yards in relief. The Vikings had entered the night with the league's top scoring defense at 13.3 points per game allowed.

stories.text: Vikings at Packers with the NFC North in play
stories.summary: Minnesota travels to Lambeau Field on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The big question is who starts at quarterback: Murray if the hamstring allows, otherwise Wentz again. The Packers are 6-3.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons lose in Madrid, sink to 3-6

stories.text: Burrow carves up Atlanta in Madrid
stories.summary: Joe Burrow went 24-for-29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns as Cincinnati beat the Falcons 34-17 on Sunday. Atlanta gave away ground with 12 penalties for 88 yards and has lost four of its last five. The Falcons sit 3-6, only a half game behind first-place Carolina.

stories.text: Hamstring trouble hangs over the Falcons
stories.summary: Defensive end Samson Ebukam and receiver Zachariah Branch both sat out the Madrid game with hamstring injuries, and coach Kevin Stefanski did not rule out Week 10 for either. Running back Brian Robinson Jr., linebacker Divine Deablo and defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. were also being monitored as of the Nov. 2 report. Watch this week's practice sheets for updates.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson stays productive in defeat
stories.summary: Bijan Robinson ran 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown against Cincinnati and added six catches for 47 yards. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. finished 20-of-31 for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception, plus 50 rushing yards.

stories.text: 13-for-18: Nick Folk's field goal line
stories.summary: Folk missed a 38-yard field goal in Madrid, his first miss inside 40 yards since Oct. 5, 2017. He has missed at least one kick in four games this season, and Stefanski sidestepped questions about a change.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Atlanta before the bye
stories.summary: Atlanta hosts Kansas City on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, then has its Week 11 bye. The Falcons lost the last meeting 22-17 in 2024. Watch whether the penalties and the kicking improve with the break coming.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers drop third straight to Denver

stories.text: Overturned pick at the 1 sinks Panthers
stories.summary: Carolina led Denver 14-13 late in the third quarter with the ball at the Broncos' 1 when a Bryce Young pass to Tommy Tremble was ruled an interception on review. Denver drove 80 yards for the lead and won 26-21. The Panthers have lost three straight, but all four NFC South teams have three wins, so they still share first place.

stories.text: Okereke sits out; Hubbard rests
stories.summary: Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) did not practice on Wednesday, and running back Chuba Hubbard sat out with a rest designation. Edge rusher Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) practiced fully, as did guard Damien Lewis (knee). The Panthers also leaned on two cornerbacks promoted from the practice squad on Sunday.

stories.text: Young throws three scores in the loss
stories.summary: Bryce Young completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns, a 106.4 passer rating. Tight end Darren Waller caught eight passes for 90 yards and a score, both season highs.

stories.text: 13: penalties for 119 yards vs. Denver
stories.summary: That total tied for the third most in franchise history. Many of the flags landed on the two cornerbacks elevated from the practice squad. Carolina still piled up 353 yards and went 3-for-3 on fourth down.

stories.text: Division showdown in the Superdome
stories.summary: Carolina visits New Orleans on Sunday, Nov. 15 at noon CT (1 p.m. ET) on Fox. Both teams are 3-5 and tied atop the NFC South. Watch the Panthers' pass protection and their penalty count.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints beat Browns in overtime, 23-22

stories.text: Shough lifts Saints past Cleveland in OT
stories.summary: Tyler Shough hit Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown on the first overtime drive, and New Orleans stopped Cleveland's two-point try to win 23-22. It was the Saints' first home win of the season and puts them at 3-5, level with every other team in the NFC South.

stories.text: Kamara, McCoy and Donaldson sit Wednesday
stories.summary: Running back Alvin Kamara (rest, back), center Erik McCoy (biceps) and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday. Travis Etienne (hamstring) and tight end Noah Fant (back) were limited.

stories.text: Shough wins it with his arm and legs
stories.summary: Shough went 21-of-35 for 265 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions, and he ran 10 times for 51 yards. He led an 11-play, 74-yard drive in overtime for the winning score.

stories.text: 4: straight games with multiple sacks for Granderson
stories.summary: Carl Granderson is the only Saint to record multiple sacks in four consecutive games, and the first NFL player to do it since 2013. New Orleans sacked Cleveland five times in all.

stories.text: Panthers come to the Superdome
stories.summary: New Orleans hosts Carolina on Sunday, Nov. 15 at noon CT (1 p.m. ET) on Fox. New kicker Charlie Smyth made three of four field goals in his debut after the Saints released Daniel Carlson, and the winner of this game takes sole possession of first place.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs fall to Bears on late field goal

stories.text: Bucs force five turnovers and still lose
stories.summary: Tampa Bay trailed 14-0, tied the game at 24 on a Bucky Irving touchdown and two-point try, and lost 27-24 when Cairo Santos kicked a 38-yard field goal at the gun. The defense intercepted Caleb Williams four times, but Baker Mayfield threw two picks, one returned 67 yards for a touchdown, and the offense went 2-for-12 on third down.

stories.text: Winfield hurts his ankle before the bye
stories.summary: Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. left the Chicago game with an ankle injury, and Ifeatu Melifonwu filled in. Receiver Emeka Egbuka returned from a two-game foot absence. The bye gives the training staff a week before the Lions game on Nov. 22.

stories.text: Irving carries the load, and Bowles notices
stories.summary: Bucky Irving ran 20 times for 97 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago. He has 111 carries in his last five games, the most by a Tampa Bay back in a five-game span since Doug Martin in 2013, and 825 rushing yards on the season. Todd Bowles says the staff will cut his carries.

stories.text: 21: takeaways, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay leads the league with 21 takeaways and 16 interceptions. Zyon McCollum has picked off a pass in three straight games, and linebacker Alex Anzalone has four interceptions, the most for any front-seven player.

stories.text: Bye week, then Detroit
stories.summary: Tampa Bay is off in Week 10. It returns at Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Bowles wants the bye used to fix turnovers, false starts and pass protection.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Minshew done, Beck likely next

stories.text: Minshew likely out for the year, Beck next in line
stories.summary: Gardner Minshew may have torn his right UCL in the 17-3 loss at Seattle and is seeking more opinions before surgery. The Cardinals drafted Carson Beck in the third round this year, and he is expected to make his first career start against the Rams. Arizona traded Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore after benching him for Minshew in Week 8.

stories.text: Minshew on IR, Wilson out with neck fracture
stories.summary: The Cardinals placed Minshew on injured reserve Tuesday. Coach Mike LaFleur said receiver Michael Wilson will miss the rest of the season with a neck fracture and also went on IR. Arizona signed Josh Johnson and Joey Aguilar from practice squads to restock the quarterback room.

stories.text: McBride caught 7 of 8 targets in a rough day
stories.summary: Tight end Trey McBride was the steadiest piece of an offense that managed only a field goal. He caught seven of eight targets for 54 yards, including a fourth-down grab late in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: 10: points in two games against Seattle this year
stories.summary: Arizona has scored a combined 10 points in its two meetings with Seattle, tying for the fewest by any team in a division season series in the last five seasons. The Seahawks have now beaten the Cardinals 11 straight times, the longest streak against one opponent in franchise history.

stories.text: Rams visit State Farm Stadium Sunday
stories.summary: Arizona hosts the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the quarterback spot, where Beck is expected to take over, and whether the Cardinals can protect him after allowing three sacks to Seattle.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams win three straight, lose Nacua

stories.text: Rams beat Washington 20-13 for a third straight win
stories.summary: Los Angeles improved to 5-4 on the road. Puka Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, Matthew Stafford hit him for the go-ahead score early in the fourth quarter, and Byron Young recovered a late fumble to seal it.

stories.text: Nacua to IR with knee ligament sprains and turf toe
stories.summary: An MRI showed a sprained MCL and PCL in Nacua's right knee plus turf toe. He is expected to miss at least a month. Davante Adams is out with a hamstring injury, guard Steve Avila is out significantly with a hamstring, and cornerback Trent McDuffie missed his third game of the season.

stories.text: Garrett posts 3 sacks in return from knee surgery
stories.summary: Myles Garrett came back after seven missed games and finished with three sacks, a forced fumble, three quarterback hits and three tackles for loss against Washington. His strip sack in the second quarter gave the Rams the ball back.

stories.text: 0-for-9: Rams on third down before the late third quarter
stories.summary: Los Angeles failed on its first nine third-down tries against Washington and converted for the first time with 2:48 left in the third quarter. The offense still scored 20 points behind Nacua's 19 targets.

stories.text: At Arizona Sunday, with Nacua and Adams out
stories.summary: The Rams visit the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. Los Angeles must find receiver production without Nacua and Adams, who combined for 100 of the team's 120 wideout catches this season.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers feast on five takeaways

stories.text: 49ers force five second-half turnovers, rout Raiders 38-17
stories.summary: San Francisco bounced back from its Week 7 loss to move to 7-1. Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown on the first play of the second half. It was the 49ers' first five-takeaway half since 2006.

stories.text: Rookie Halton out for season with broken ankle
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Gracen Halton broke his left ankle late in the win and leaves after 15 tackles and two sacks in eight games. Cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) also left the game, and Kyle Shanahan said more testing is coming. Nate Hobbs could return from IR against Dallas.

stories.text: Purdy reaches 100 touchdown passes in 57 games
stories.summary: Brock Purdy threw two touchdown passes, including a 37-yarder to Jordan Watkins, and ran for another score. He became the 10th quarterback since the merger to reach 100 career touchdown passes in his first 57 games.

stories.text: 6: straight games Las Vegas has allowed 30 or more points
stories.summary: The Raiders tied an NFL record by giving up at least 30 points for a sixth straight game. San Francisco added to the pile with 38, and Fred Warner forced one fumble and recovered another.

stories.text: At Dallas Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: San Francisco visits the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox at AT&T Stadium. The injury report on the secondary and defensive line is the thing to watch after Week 9.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Lock steadies Seahawks again

stories.text: Lock and Barner lead Seattle past Arizona 17-3
stories.summary: Drew Lock, starting for the injured Sam Darnold, went 19 of 28 for 175 yards and a touchdown. Tight end A.J. Barner scored twice, once on a catch and once on a run, and Seattle improved to 5-4 with a season sweep of the Cardinals.

stories.text: Darnold out again, Lock managing oblique and quad
stories.summary: Mike Macdonald said Lock will start Sunday in Las Vegas. Darnold, who has a cracked rib and a quad injury, is week to week and may return after the Week 11 bye. Left guard Quenton Nelson had a knee procedure and will miss the Raiders game.

stories.text: Smith-Njigba tops 1,000 yards through nine games
stories.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught seven passes for 51 yards against Arizona and now has 1,036 receiving yards. He is the third Seahawk with three straight 1,000-yard seasons, joining Tyler Lockett and Steve Largent.

stories.text: 11: straight wins over Arizona
stories.summary: Seattle has beaten the Cardinals 11 times in a row, the longest streak against one opponent in team history. The defense held Arizona to 198 yards and 3 points, and Derick Hall had a career-high three tackles for loss.

stories.text: At Las Vegas Sunday, then the bye
stories.summary: Seattle plays the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS at Allegiant Stadium, then has its Week 11 bye. Watch whether Lock's oblique and the missing offensive line pieces hold up.
